from.place: Unique cohomology-normalized identification with a degree-zero object

title: Unique cohomology-normalized identification with a degree-zero object
statement: For an abelian category C with a derived category, let X be an object with H^q(X)=0 for q≠0. There exists a unique isomorphism e:X≅single(H^0(X)) such that H^0(e) followed by the standard single-cohomology comparison is the identity of H^0(X). This is valid for every abelian category, including the zero category.

source.place: The concentration, overlap, and degree-zero gluing argument

proof.text: Use Mathlib isGE_iff and isLE_iff to put X in degree zero, and exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE to choose e:X≅single(Y).
Compose with the single image of the inverse of H^0(e) followed by the standard single-H^0 comparison. Its naturality proves that the new isomorphism induces the identity.
For uniqueness, use full faithfulness of singleFunctor and faithfulness of its composition with H^0. Cancel the chosen inverse to compare the two isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_single_homology_zero
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C]
    (X : DerivedCategory C)
    (hX : ∀ q : ℤ, q ≠ 0 → IsZero ((homologyFunctor C q).obj X)) :
    ∃! e : X ≅ (singleFunctor C 0).obj ((homologyFunctor C 0).obj X),
      (homologyFunctor C 0).map e.hom ≫
        (singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso C 0).hom.app ((homologyFunctor C 0).obj X) =
      𝟙 ((homologyFunctor C 0).obj X)
